reason: The pinned Codex native protocol exposes rerouting and configured thread settings. Continuous guards must cover these events without inventing provider-internal model telemetry.

cases.expected: A model/rerouted frame from the owned native stream refuses before tool routing, retains the first model and records its actual source; the controller does not retry around the provider refusal.
Changed configured model or requested effort in thread/settings/updated fences queued file or command effects; unchanged model names in assistant text do not affect the guard.

Changes or unknown values for modelProvider, cwd, approvalPolicy, approvalsReviewer, sandboxPolicy or collaboration model/effort refuse. readOnly with networkAccess=true is not accepted as the sealed policy.
An identical settings notification is idempotent; the original startup receipt, observed model, sources and expiry remain unchanged.

A foreign, missing or malformed thread identity on a profile notification cannot establish or replace owned-thread evidence. Ambiguous owned-stream configuration is refused without claiming the foreign model was executed.
The correlated thread/start response must acknowledge the requested model and effort and constrained execution settings. A mismatching or missing requested effort refuses before readiness.

An unsolicited thread-shaped response cannot mint profile binding. Durable binding records must resolve their signed owned native source and match the correlated result; missing or inconsistent source refuses.
A reroute or changed settings frame remains a refusal when a new observer or verifier reads the same owned history. An earlier valid startup cannot hide a later change.
Assistant text, task prose and nested notification-shaped content do not become native configuration events.
The configured model and effort are recorded as native thread acknowledgements, with provider-internal execution model and actual execution effort null when the protocol does not expose them.
Settings observed before a correlated thread/start can be checked against that eventual thread but cannot independently grant effects; foreign pending scope or unresolved binding refuses.

scope: Mechanical owned-process frames and controller-source validation only. No account, thread or model operation; no reopening of the failed live packet.
